html:
Roman emperor from 54 to 68 CE, the last of the Julio-Claudian dynasty, remembered as a tyrant who loved the stage.

He was the son of Agrippina the Younger, who married the emperor Claudius and got Nero adopted as heir. He became emperor at sixteen. His first years, guided by Seneca and the guard commander Burrus, were seen as good. Then he had his stepbrother Britannicus poisoned and, in 59 CE, his mother killed.

He sang, played the lyre and drove chariots in public, which shocked the upper classes, and toured Greece to compete in its festivals. When the Great Fire of 64 CE destroyed much of Rome, rumours blamed him, and he blamed the Christians, starting the first persecution of Christians in Rome. On the burned land he built his Golden House.

His reign also saw Boudica's revolt in Britain and the Jewish revolt in Judaea. In 68 CE governors in Gaul and Spain rebelled, the Senate declared him a public enemy, and he killed himself, saying, it is reported, "What an artist dies in me!" The Year of the Four Emperors followed.
sum: Roman emperor from 54 to 68 CE, the last of the Julio-Claudian dynasty, remembered as a tyrant who loved the stage.
